clue.text: Lofted stroke out to sea produces Franco-British food

parts.note: a ball that is lofted has been chipped, as in golf

indicators.note: letters that are out are scattered or put out of place, so the next words get rearranged

parts.note: a pot is a stroke in snooker or billiards
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer's high shot sails out over the sea, somehow producing a dish shared by France and Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Chipped potatoes are chips, which the French eat as frites, hence a food both countries claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried potato strips are eaten on both sides of the Channel, as frites in France and as chips in Britain.

clue.text: "Pisces" could be applied to men or fish — or penguins

indicators.note: saying the letters could be something else invites rearranging them into another word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled wonder whether the star sign of the Fishes fits people, fish, or even penguins.
explanation.walkthrough: SPHENISCIFORMES is the zoological order containing all the penguins; the fifteen letters of the fodder are exactly those needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The scientific order name groups every species of flightless Antarctic seabird, so it stands for the birds collectively.

clue.text: Join as first officer on the "Morning Seaweed"

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits below it, so it comes last

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning
an alga is a seaweed
the first mate is a ship's first officer

explanation.surface: Someone signs on as first mate aboard a ship called the Morning Seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: To amalgamate is to merge or combine separate things into one, a synonym for uniting them.

clue.text: Stuff on the road makes snake stop

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
to halt is to stop

explanation.surface: A snake lying across the road brings the traffic to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the tarry surfacing material laid down on highways, so it is literally material on a carriageway.

clue.text: See 17
Went to church, there being no need for 13 8

definitions.meaning: first meaning: was present at a religious service
second meaning: a petrol station where staff fill your tank, so customers need not man the pumps themselves

explanation.surface: A churchgoer's attendance makes an emergency call for all hands unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 8 is ALL HANDS TO THE PUMPS; at an attended-service garage an attendant works the pump, unlike at a self-service one.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to a church service is attending it, and attended service is the trade term for forecourts staffed by pump attendants.

clue.text: Hell's gate, chaps! It's time for the waving of a wand

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld and Dante's city of Hell
a gate is an entrance
chaps are men
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A pantomime magician tells his men at the gates of Hell that it is time for the magic wand.
explanation.walkthrough: Disentrancement is the breaking of a trance or spell, as a fairy-tale wand does.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave of the magic wand traditionally releases someone from an enchantment, which is exactly the act of breaking a trance.

clue.text: See 13
Outside the teepee stands the Foreign Office minister, a capital fixer

indicators.note: one thing standing outside another wraps around it on both sides

parts.note: Peter Hain was a Foreign Office minister when this was published in 2000
teepee sounds like the letters T and P said in turn

explanation.surface: A government minister stands outside a wigwam that houses some fixer from the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital here means of the head, as in capital punishment; a hatpin fixes a hat to the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatpin is a long pin that secures a hat to the wearer's hair, so it fastens something worn on the head.

clue.text: Second visit to court has charm

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a case taken to a higher court for another hearing

explanation.surface: Going back to court a second time has a certain charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal appeal asks a higher court to rehear a case, and appeal is also the quality of being attractive.

clue.text: I'm dashed — the female's gone in to be publicised

indicators.note: something that has gone in is now sitting inside another word

parts.note: hyped means heavily publicised
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in dismay that a woman has gone inside just to get publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm dashed' sounds like an oath, but it is a compound word speaking: it has been joined with a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphened word is joined to another by a short dash, so a compound in the first person could say it has been dashed.

clue.text: The trouser tribe?

parts.note: surface reading: a group of people defined by their trousers
setter's reading: one of the twelve tribes of Israel whose name is also a famous brand of jeans

explanation.walkthrough: Levi's is the American jeans maker, and Levi is one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: The tribe of Levi shares its name with a denim brand, so it is the Biblical tribe with trouser connections.

clue.text: Held maths with laptop unsporting? The 5 is 17!

indicators.note: porting means turning a ship's helm to port, so the letters are swung about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the last word splits as uns-porting, and only its opening letters join the fodder

explanation.surface: A cry of alarm at someone hogging the maths with a laptop, then an announcement that the ship is sinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'unsporting' as uns-porting: the letters UNS join the fodder and porting, a nautical turn, stirs them. 5 17 is SINKING SHIP, so the definition says the ship is sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: When a ship is going down, the traditional emergency call summons every crew member to work the pumps.

clue.text: The whole personality to be elevated by what Bunyan did

definitions.note: past tense, while the answer is the bare verb

indicators.note: one thing elevated by another has the second placed beneath it, after it in a down entry

parts.note: the whole is all
the ego is the self or personality
to be elevated is to rise

explanation.surface: Someone's whole character is lifted up by reading what John Bunyan wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bunyan wrote The Pilgrim's Progress, the best-known allegory in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunyan told a moral story through symbolic characters and journeys, which is what turning something into an allegory means.

clue.text: Particular place is required

indicators.note: read as re-quired, the words are gathered up again in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fussy person insists on having a certain place.
explanation.definitionFit: Special and particular are synonyms meaning specific, singled out from the general run.

clue.text: Free held, with a ring around the 'ead and face

indicators.note: the apostrophe shows a Cockney dropping the aitch, so the same must be done to the word it describes

parts.note: a halo is a ring of light around the head
dial is slang for face

explanation.surface: A saint is pictured with a halo around a dropped-aitch head and face.
explanation.walkthrough: Alodial (or allodial) land is owned outright, not held from a feudal lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Allodial tenure means owning land absolutely, with no overlord, so the property is possessed without obligation.

clue.text: 21 23 the "Napoleon of crime" to ending of abstraction

definitions.note: the answer completes the saying rats desert the sinking ship

parts.note: the emperor of crime read as the monarch of wrongdoing: sin plus king
-ship is a suffix forming abstract nouns, as in friendship

explanation.surface: Fleeing rodents abandon Moriarty for some abstract conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 23 is RATS DESERT. Sherlock Holmes called Moriarty the Napoleon of crime; here it is taken literally as a king of sin.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says rats desert the sinking ship, so the answer fills the gap after the cross-referenced words.

clue.text: Row 9's back, entering the specific gravity of starch

indicators.note: the pieces go into the following letters

parts.note: SG is the abbreviation for specific gravity
a tiff is a row or quarrel

indicators.note: something sent back runs the other way, right to left

parts.note: the number written as a word

explanation.surface: An argument about the heaviness of laundry starch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 here is the number itself, not the 9-across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is the substance used to stiffen collars and shirts, so it is a stiffening agent.

clue.text: Everyone goes in for teaching

indicators.note: the answer goes inside the following word, sitting within its letters

parts.note: the inner letters of this word

explanation.surface: Everybody chooses a career in teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Each and everyone both refer to every member of a group taken individually.

clue.text: French writer entertaining model monarch on journey by 5

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it
a host entertaining a guest holds it inside

parts.note: Jean-Paul Sartre, the French philosopher and novelist
the Model T was Ford's famous car
K is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Sartre plays host to a king who arrives as a model on a sea voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is SHIP, so the journey is by starship, as the Enterprise travels in the TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: The television series follows the voyages of the starship Enterprise, so a trek among the stars is a trip by space vessel.

clue.text: See 23
Smarten up the parson if he's going to take a seat?

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a parson's title
taken as written
an MP takes a seat in Parliament

explanation.surface: A parson standing for Parliament had better tidy himself up first.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers a parson becoming a Member of Parliament: Rev, a, MP.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp is to renovate or give a fresh look, much as tidying up improves appearance.

clue.text: Monty's creatures get their dues without art forgery

indicators.note: without means outside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: just deserts are what someone deserves

indicators.note: a forgery is a fake made over, so the letters are remade

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Montgomery's men get what's coming to them, minus any art fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: Monty is Field Marshal Montgomery, whose Eighth Army in North Africa were nicknamed the Desert Rats.
explanation.definitionFit: The Desert Rats were the 7th Armoured Division under Montgomery, named after their jerboa emblem.

clue.text: Not a soul keeps dry in front of the spacecraft

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it within

parts.note: not a soul means no one
sec is French for dry, used of wine

explanation.surface: Nobody stays dry up at the front of a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose cone is the pointed forward section of a rocket or missile, which leads it through the air.
